newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Malaysia deals, Thai Danu delay.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Malaysia deals, Thai Danu delay.

text.p: Asian debt markets offered few new issues on Wednesday but plenty of news of issues, with Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia all attracting notice.
Malaysia's Berjaya is enjoying strong demand for its US$100 million floating rate note issue launched Tuesday.
The five-year notes pay an all-in of 148 basis points, toward the low end of the indicated 145-165 basis point range.
Malaysian issuers are a rarity in the international capital markets and that is one reason for the issue's appeal, a syndicate manager at arranger Chase Manhattan Asia said.
Some bankers predict that Malaysian issues may become even more infrequent as the country's already strict rules governing foreign borrowing tighten further.
Tenaga is in the midst of taking bids for a planned Yankee bond, which is expected to be some US$500 million in size.

The mandate will be restricted to banks that have a presence in Labuan, Malaysia's offshore financial centre. That group would include the commercial banks or possibly those investment banks that have set up joint ventures with Labuan entities.
A few U.S. investment banks reportedly have set up such joint ventures.
Some bankers said they suspect Tenaga's decision to go through a Labuan bank is a response to the government's apparent plans to nix a withholding tax exemption for overseas borrowing.
But others said that Bank Negara recently has been pushing borrowers to use Labuan and that approval for the issue depends on going that route.
"Tenaga is pushing both for approval and for the tax withholding exemption," said one banker.
The Berjaya issue avoided this process because it was launched through an offshore special purpose vehicle and because its proceeds will be used for offshore purposes, bankers said.

Petronas also managed to get around Labuan in its recent issues--its highly successful $1.9 billion global launched last year through Salomon Brothers and a more recent Samurai issue-- because they were mandated months ago.
The Petronas global bond specifically included a clause including a special tax redemption in case Malaysia did impose withholding taxes.

Some bankers speculated that the setting up of joint ventures in Labuan by investment banks may give them access to the Malaysian market in the short term, but that a bigger presence could be required in future.
"The investment banks may set up a joint venture, but the Malaysian government could set new rules," said a banker.
"If they want to emphasise the development of local markets, they may want companies to set up full branch operations in Labuan," he said.
Meanwhile, Thai Danu Bank announced that it had delayed completion of its US$130 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue because of its planned merger with Finance One.
The two-tranche FRCD issue was launched on February 25. The issue's outlook turned sour on news of the merger because of uncertainty over Finance One's loan portfolio.
Analysts said that determining Finance One's bad loan situation is difficult, partly because of poor disclosure in Thailand and partly because of the way loans are treated on the balance sheet.
Elsewhere, Riaupulp said that it would enter into talks with significant holders of its funding unit RAPP Finance's bonds.
The lone launch today was a 7.0 billion yen bond for the Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand via Lehman Brothers.
